title: CSP Bypass via Missing base-uri Directive
learning_objectives: Understand that a CSP script-src allowlist governs WHERE scripts load from, while the base-uri directive governs how RELATIVE script URLs resolve — omitting base-uri leaves a hole even under a tight script-src 'self'
Exploit a <base href> injection: changing the document base URL repoints every relative resource, including <script src="main.js">, at a location the attacker controls
Keep the redirected script SAME-ORIGIN so it still satisfies script-src 'self' — a user-content path on your own origin (uploads, a JSONP echo, a cache) is enough; you do not need a foreign host
Recognise that ordinary same-origin user content becomes script execution the moment a relative <script src> can be repointed at it via base-uri
Apply the fix: always set base-uri 'none' (or 'self') alongside a script-src allowlist, and prefer absolute paths / SRI for first-party bundles
flag_hint: The CSP is script-src 'self' with NO base-uri, and the page loads a RELATIVE <script src="main.js"> below a reflected ?ref= injection in <head>. Upload your JS (POST /upload -> served same-origin at /u/<id>/main.js), then queue /?ref=<base href="/u/<id>/"> — the injected base makes main.js resolve to your same-origin upload (still 'self'), which runs and can read document.cookie. Beacon it, read /oob/received, POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: CSP script-src 'self' with NO base-uri directive (the flaw)
same-origin upload path /u/<id>/main.js as the base-uri hijack target
inspired_by: The documented base-uri / <base> hijack of relative-path scripts under CSP (Terjanq, Cure53 and the CSP base-uri guidance), abstracted for local Docker with a Flask target that omits base-uri, a same-origin upload path, a Playwright admin bot, and an OOB collector
